content.text: bisphos may be considered for pain in early CRPS, esp w abnorm bone scans; sm RCTs: alendronate · neridronate & clodronate can ↓pain, w generally mild SE; consider serious risks: ONJ · esophageal ulceration

CI: esophageal abnormalities that delay esophageal emptying (stricture or achalasia). CI: inability to stand or sit upright ≥ 30 min. CI: hypocalcemia. Esophageal rxns (esophagitis · ulcers · erosions) reported - be alert for signs & instruct pts to d/c & seek medical attention for dysphagia · odynophagia · retrosternal pain or new/worsening heartburn. Hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Severe bone · joint · musc pain may occur - d/c use if severe Sx develop. ONJ reported (can occur spontaneously; generally assoc w tooth extraction and/or local infect w delayed heal). Atypical frx incl femoral frx reported - pts w new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to r/o femoral frx - re-evaluate risk/benefit & consider interrupting bisphos therapy. ⍉recommended if CrCl < 35 mL/min. Calcium · antacids or PO meds containing multivalent cations interfere w absorb - instruct pts to wait ≥ ½ hr after FOSAMAX b4 any other PO med. OD: hypocalcemia · hypophosphatemia & upper GI adverse events may result - give milk or antacids to bind alendronate - ⍉ induce vomiting (risk of esophageal irritate) - keep the pt fully upright
